skill.name: lark-workflow-meeting-summary
skill.description: Summarizes Lark meeting minutes for a chosen time range and prepares a structured meeting report.
skill.summary: Creates daily or weekly Lark meeting minute summaries from VC, note, Drive, and document data.
skill.author: larksuite

security_audit.summary: The skill is a Lark CLI workflow that intentionally runs commands to read meeting, note, Drive, and document data. Most Markdown backtick and reconnaissance hits are false positives, but parent-relative reads cross the skill package boundary and document write examples need safer content handling.

remediation.issue: Parent-relative references require reading sibling skill files outside this package.
remediation.suggestion: Inline the required guidance or package audited reference files inside this skill directory.

remediation.issue: Document creation examples embed generated report content inside shell-quoted arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Use a file, stdin, or a documented escaping strategy for document content passed to lark-cli.

remediation.issue: The workflow accesses meeting notes, transcript data, document tokens, and optional document writes.
remediation.suggestion: State required permissions and ask for confirmation before transcript retrieval or document creation.

semantic_findings.title: Cross-Package Skill Dependency
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md tells the agent to read sibling skill files using parent-relative paths before running the workflow. This can import unaudited instructions outside the packaged skill and makes the skill non-self-contained.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines directly use ../ paths and mandatory read wording. The concern is the instruction-boundary dependency, not arbitrary path input.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Shell Content Construction
semantic_findings.description: The document creation examples place generated report content inside shell-quoted command arguments. Meeting text can contain quotes or shell metacharacters, so authors should specify file-based or stdin-based input.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The risk depends on how the agent substitutes content, but the example gives no escaping or safer input method.

content.value_statement: Meeting records are hard to review across many Lark calls. This skill gathers meeting metadata, note links, and transcript context into a structured report.
actual_capabilities: Determines a date range for daily, weekly, or custom meeting reviews.
Searches Lark VC meetings through lark-cli commands.
Retrieves note IDs and document tokens for meeting minutes.
Fetches document metadata and share links through Drive metadata queries.
Formats daily or weekly meeting reports with missing-note status.
Optionally creates or updates a Lark document when requested.
limitations: Requires authenticated lark-cli access for VC, Drive, and Docs data.
Relies on related Lark skill references that may not be packaged here.
Cannot summarize meetings when notes or transcripts are unavailable.
Searches longer than one month must be split into smaller ranges.

use_cases.title: Prepare a weekly meeting review
use_cases.description: Collect all meetings from the past week and produce a report with links and missing-note status.

use_cases.title: Create a daily executive digest
use_cases.description: Summarize today’s Lark meetings with times, topics, note links, and transcript availability.

use_cases.title: Track project discussion history
use_cases.description: Review a custom date range and group meeting records for planning, follow-up, and audit needs.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize this week
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize my Lark meetings from this week. Include meeting times, topics, note links, and missing notes.

prompt_templates.title: Create today’s digest
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a digest for today’s Lark meetings. Separate meetings with notes from meetings without notes.

prompt_templates.title: Review a custom range
prompt_templates.prompt: Review Lark meetings from the last 14 days. Group results by day and highlight transcript availability.

prompt_templates.title: Publish a Lark report
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a Lark meeting report for the past month. Confirm the destination document before creating or updating it.

output_examples.input: Summarize meetings from the past seven days.
output_examples.output: A weekly report with meeting counts, each meeting title, note links, transcript status, and items needing follow-up.
A daily overview with meeting times, topics, available minutes, missing notes, and unified-note transcript notes.
A date-grouped report that separates completed meeting notes from meetings that require manual transcript retrieval.

best_practices: Confirm the date range and timezone before running meeting searches.
Use least-privilege Lark authorization for only the needed domains.
Ask before creating or updating Lark documents.
anti_patterns: Do not search broad date ranges without a pagination and batching plan.
Do not share transcript or document links with unauthorized recipients.
Do not create documents before confirming the destination and audience.

faq.question: Does this skill require lark-cli?
faq.answer: Yes. It depends on lark-cli for meeting search, note lookup, Drive metadata, and document actions.

faq.question: Can it create a Lark document?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create or update a document when the user asks and confirms the destination.

faq.question: What happens when a meeting has no notes?
faq.answer: The report marks the meeting as having no minutes, so users can follow up manually.

faq.question: Can it summarize long date ranges?
faq.answer: Yes, but searches longer than one month must be split into separate query windows.

faq.question: Does it fetch full transcripts?
faq.answer: Only when transcript data is needed and the authenticated user has permission to access it.

faq.question: What permissions are needed?
faq.answer: The user needs Lark permissions for VC meetings, notes, Drive metadata, and optional document creation.
